explanation: A token-identity detector for a fixed, semantically mixed word list: it fires on the word itself, in any syntactic role (after 'was', after 'a'/'the', as subject or object), once at least about three tokens of text precede it: the deceit and mortality words lie/lies/lying/lied, dies/dying/death/suicide/mourning, guilty, punishment, arrest, and also comforting, nearest, winning, statement, holding, donating, and the second subword piece of split words such as b|itten, st|umbling, how|ling, Can|oe, To|ys, Compar|isons, plus LaTeX \sum. These reach about 0.3-1.0 of max, and an immediately preceding copula or linking verb (was, seemed, found him) adds roughly a third more. It stays below about 0.15 of max on function words, punctuation, colour words (red, blue, green, white, black), ready/early/late/busy/big, the crime-neighbour words trial, verdict and liar, and the same list words when they are the first or second token of the text. Ordinary nouns, verbs and adjectives that are not on the list are unclaimed: they mostly stay under 0.2 of max outside copula frames but can reach 0.2-0.4 after 'was'/'seemed' (cold, old, dog, family, meeting, crime). Text-initial My/Our/Your/Three/When also reach about 0.3 of max.
